newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan new commod exchange to mull listing index.
newsitem.headline: Japan new commod exchange to mull listing index.

text.p: The newly established Chubo Commodity Exchange in central Japan, said on Tuesday that it was considering establishing an overall commodity index listing both agricultural and textile products.

"By merging the three Nagoya-area exchanges, we have for the first time an exchange that transcends the boundaries of the Agriculture Ministry and the Trade Ministry, and we're thinking of taking advantage of that," exchange president Hanshichi Toyoshima said on Tuesday.

Japan's commodities exchanges have up to now limited themselves either to agricultural goods, if they were under the jurisdiction of the Agriculture Ministry, or to industrial commodities, if they were supervised by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry.
The Nagoya Textile Exchange, the Nagoya Grain and Sugar Exchange and the Toyohashi Dry Cocoon Exchange merged into one exchange called Chubo Commodity Exchange as of Tuesday.
Falling trading volumes and market share in comparison to Tokyo-based exchanges forced the merger.
